title: Limit length of lag detector hot threads log lines

timeline.message:
Limit length of lag detector hot threads log lines

If debug logging is enabled then the lag detector will capture and
report the hot threads of a lagging node. In some cases the resulting
log message can be very large, exceeding 10kiB, which means it is
truncated in most logging setups. The relevant thread(s) may be waiting
on I/O, which is not considered "hot" and therefore may not appear in
the first 10kiB.

This commit adjusts this logging mechanism to split the message into
chunks of size at most 2kiB (after compression and base64-encoding) to
ensure that the entire hot threads output can be faithfully
reconstructed from these logs.

Closes #88126
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.body: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

I am not sure if there could be many of these tasks piling up in the prioritized thread runner, but just in case, would it make sense to capture the timestamp on task creation and use it to prioritize earlier tasks higher?

reply.body: They shouldn't pile up much, but even if they do it's a `PriorityBlockingQueue` which yields tasks of equal priority in FIFO order.

timeline.body: Would it make sense to make this an undocumented configurable setting?

reply.body: This functionality only really makes sense for debugging, and I don't see a great reason to want to change this.

I've thought about this a little more and I now see value in adding some configurability here. Particularly the `NodesHotThreadsRequest` we use has some hard-coded parameters & defaults that deserve to be exposed as settings, and if we're adding those settings then why not this one too?

I won't do it in this PR tho, nor do I expect to get to it any time soon, but if you're interested then feel free to open a follow-up.

I think 2KiB is reasonable. And since now we have some quick commands to reconstruct it, I think it is fine. Originally I had thought (before I realized of the econding) that I could have set this to something large, so that there would be one big block of human-readable text. But since now either way we need to process the encoded text, I do not mind the chunks. We can make this configurable if the need ever arises.

timeline.body: This description has similar text to the class description. Maybe consolidate in one place?

reply.body: I think we need Javadoc in both places. Is there a way to share common chunks of Javadoc?
Could link to the class or link the function from the class, but it is not that important.

timeline.body: Does this mean the new lag output will not be human-readable text anymore? I am not keen about the fact that semi-manual reconstruction will be required.

reply.body:
Yes, that's deliberate. We have scripts that process hot threads output, but they don't work so well if it gets mangled (e.g. whitespace lost) on the way to us. I also intend to try using this for #38939, which would involve capturing non-ASCII data that won't translate well in logs. Again, this is only really for debugging, and it's pretty trivial to decode this ~(e.g. `:%!gzip -d|base64 -D` in vi).~

Lol hoist by my own petard. I meant `:%!base64 -D|gzip -d`. Pretty trivial my foot.

I see. I have seen the LagDetector's output in issues and it is quite useful in a human-readable form. If we change it, I would appreciate if you can:

* Modify the [relevant documentation](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/8.6/cluster-fault-detection.html#_diagnosing_lagging_nodes) to mention an easy way to decode it into human-readable format (maybe with the `vi` command you mentioned, or better yet some terminal commands to do it).
* Maybe also write the same command in the final line logged, so it is easy for a human to try to decode it to a human-readable form.

I understand that for debugging purposes, there may be tools that will do all this automatically, but I feel that it will be useful also for less experienced humans to get the human-readable output.
Just because I feel a bit uneasy on this, @tlrx feel free to comment as well. I'd feel better if at least 2 people are fine with the encoded output :)
Would an alternative be to store the lag log in a separate log file? E.g., configure a log4j configuration so the LagDetector's log goes into a separate file?

Fair point, see a93504724c1c2a7325c2e624302b3406e4bddb7d.

If we put it in a separate file it would be much less likely to be shared with us. For instance, in Cloud we would have to change the whole log indexing pipeline to handle the new file, and experience shows that on-prem folks are sometimes pretty bad at sharing the info we need even when it's in a standard place and format.
Thanks for the explanation, that makes sense. I like the documentation changes.

timeline.body: I guess the standard charset here encompasses all the safe bytes mentioned below?

reply.body: Yes, [ISO-8859-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_8859-1) agrees with US-ASCII (and hence UTF-8) on these bytes, and is the encoding that Java uses internally which makes this the most efficient way to construct a `String` from some bytes.

timeline.body: I guess here you're trying to test different lengths around the chunk size?
I like the splitting, however I am not sure about the encoding. I would prefer human-readable chunks I think.

@@ -201,7 +201,26 @@ logger.org.elasticsearch.cluster.coordination.LagDetector: DEBUG
 
 When this logger is enabled, {es} will attempt to run the
 <<cluster-nodes-hot-threads>> API on the faulty node and report the results in
-the logs on the elected master.
+the logs on the elected master. The results are compressed, encoded, and split
+into chunks to avoid truncation:
+
+[source,text]
+----
+[DEBUG][o.e.c.c.LagDetector      ] [master] hot threads from node [{node}{g3cCUaMDQJmQ2ZLtjr-3dg}{10.0.0.1:9300}] lagging at version [183619] despite commit of cluster state version [183620] [part 1]: H4sIAAAAAAAA/x...
+[DEBUG][o.e.c.c.LagDetector      ] [master] hot threads from node [{node}{g3cCUaMDQJmQ2ZLtjr-3dg}{10.0.0.1:9300}] lagging at version [183619] despite commit of cluster state version [183620] [part 2]: p7x3w1hmOQVtuV...
+[DEBUG][o.e.c.c.LagDetector      ] [master] hot threads from node [{node}{g3cCUaMDQJmQ2ZLtjr-3dg}{10.0.0.1:9300}] lagging at version [183619] despite commit of cluster state version [183620] [part 3]: v7uTboMGDbyOy+...
+[DEBUG][o.e.c.c.LagDetector      ] [master] hot threads from node [{node}{g3cCUaMDQJmQ2ZLtjr-3dg}{10.0.0.1:9300}] lagging at version [183619] despite commit of cluster state version [183620] [part 4]: 4tse0RnPnLeDNN...
+[DEBUG][o.e.c.c.LagDetector      ] [master] hot threads from node [{node}{g3cCUaMDQJmQ2ZLtjr-3dg}{10.0.0.1:9300}] lagging at version [183619] despite commit of cluster state version [183620] (gzip compressed, base64-encoded, and split into 4 parts on preceding log lines)
+----
+
+To reconstruct the output, base64-decode the data and decompress it using
+`gzip`. For instance, on Unix-like systems:
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+cat lagdetector.log | sed -e 's/.*://' | base64 --decode | gzip --decompress
+----
+// NOTCONSOLE
 
 ===== Diagnosing `follower check retry count exceeded` nodes
